source.post_text:
People open apps for 2 reasons:

(1) Perform useful actions
(2) Consume entertaining content

No consumer in the history of time has ever opened an app to experience a microinteraction

replies.text: 😂😂 except the guy from the take my money meme
replies.author: @imranscripts

replies.text: Well,  like, favorite, reactions, they all have something in common, right?
replies.author: @mironcatalin

replies.text:
true, but I think delight and micro interactions are like free surface area to get people to share / talk about your product 

it should meet either 1) or 2) first though
replies.author: @r1thv1ka

replies.text: microinteractions can be part of what makes a good app sticky, especially for the first 15 minutes of exploring an app
replies.author: @puravmanot

replies.text: Fair point overall, though I'd argue microinteractions quietly support those two goals by making actions feel smoother and content more engaging without users ever seeking them out directly.
replies.author: decoy

decoy_rationale: The reply feels slightly too balanced and explanatory in one neat sentence, hedging like a mini-essay rather than a quick casual take.
